title: Preparing U.S. Land Forces to Fight in an Era of Strategic and Technological Disruption
gist: CSIS working paper assesses Army and Marine Corps modernization across force structure, recruitment/training and acquisition, concluding the most pressing needs are deeper munitions stockpiles, faster unmanned/autonomous adoption and a tighter industry feedback loop.

insights.claim: The Marine Corps has committed to a defined operational vision through Force Design and accepted hard divest-to-invest trade-offs, whereas the Army's 'How the Army Fights' guidance links doctrine and design but still leaves roles at each echelon and global posture choices unresolved.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Marine divestments signal where land-force capital is shifting; Army posture decisions remain a source of budget uncertainty.

insights.claim: The Army carries a disproportionate share of joint executive agency responsibilities, primary responsibility for logistics and sustainment, and a vital role in air defense, making it a central enabler of the joint force.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Enabler roles (logistics, air defense) imply sustained demand for sustainment and air-defense programs.

insights.claim: Both services face the fiscal legacy of post-Cold War and post-GWOT drawdowns, competing personnel versus procurement demands, and a difficult recruiting environment while integrating new technology into training.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Personnel costs crowd out procurement; watch budget tradeoffs.

insights.claim: The most pressing land-force acquisition needs are deeper munitions stockpiles, faster adoption of unmanned and autonomous systems, and a tighter feedback loop with industry.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Points to demand tailwinds for munitions producers and autonomy suppliers.
insights.quote: Their most pressing acquisition needs are deeper munitions stockpiles, faster adoption of unmanned and autonomous systems, and a tighter feedback loop with industry.

insights.claim: Unmanned systems, stand-off precision strikes and contested logistics are challenging long-standing assumptions about how land forces prevail on the battlefield.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Technology shift reorders force-structure priorities away from legacy platforms.

top_entities: Association of the United States Army
